Good morning, everyone. Here is a short summary of our quarterly report. This quarter, more iron was produced than last year: our output grew by eight percent. Most of it is sold to steel companies in Brazil, and ten percent is exported to China. On the fruit side, the harvest was very good. The mangoes were picked in October, and three shipments were sent to Europe. One shipment was delayed by bad weather, but it arrived safely two weeks later. The annual audit was completed in March, and the findings were positive. No serious problems were found. All the numbers are shown in the chart on page three. Thank you. Questions are welcome at the end.

Let me explain how our fruit gets from the farm to Europe. First, the mangoes are picked by hand in the early morning. Then they are taken to the packing house, where they are washed and checked. Bad fruit is removed. After that, the good mangoes are packed in boxes of four kilos. Each box is labeled with the farm name and the date. Next, the boxes are loaded into cold containers. The containers are driven to the port of Santos, and from there they are shipped to Rotterdam. The trip takes about three weeks. When the fruit arrives, it is checked again by the client. Last year, more than two hundred containers were sent this way, and only two were rejected.

First, the numbers are collected from the plant and the farms. Then, the data is checked by the finance team. Next, the charts are prepared for the report. After that, the report is reviewed and approved by the director. Finally, the report is sent to the board of directors.
